notes:
- Account wants production-grade Dedicated with strict throughput guarantees (not just best-effort).
- Primary ask: minimum tokens/sec per reserved pool, expressed as sustained rate over 5m and 1h windows.
- Secondary ask: explicit concurrency caps per model route to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.
- Burst policy: they will accept short bursts (30s–2m) up to 2x sustained rate if documented and billable or throttled; legal wants hard limits and pre-warn thresholds.
- POC: staging reserve = 8x A100-eq GPUs; metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU util, KV cache hit rate.
- Pricing: prefer blended committed rate with separate overage for bursts; Redwood pricing deck under review (drive:/deals/maplecrest/2026/pricing-deck-v3.pdf).
- Quote from CTO on 2026-02-23 call: "We need deterministic throughput — our checkout assistant drives conversions and cannot degrade during peak sales windows."
- Engineering note: need clarity whether KV/prefix cache reduces token accounting for guarantees (SE notes: cache hits still count for latency but not tokens generated).
- They require SSO/SAML, audit logs to be retained for 7 years, and EU region data residency for EU customers only (hybrid residency).
- Potential upsell: Optimize tooling to tune batching/quantization after go-live.
- Timeline sensitivity: want contract in place before Q2 marketing campaign (April).
procurement_details:
- Proposed commitment: 1-year reserved cluster, 8 A100-equivalent nodes, with option to increase to 12 nodes after 6 months.
- Billing: monthly invoice against committed spend + metered overage.
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool; p95 latency SLOs tied to credits; minimum sustained throughput guarantee clause requested.
- Proposed minimum tokens/sec: 12,000 sustained (5m avg) across generation route, with guaranteed per-session concurrency cap = 20.
- Burst policy draft: allowed burst multiplier = 2x for up to 120 seconds; bursts beyond that subject to throttling or negotiated overage billing.
- Acceptance criteria for handover: performance test reproducible on Redwood staging cluster and signed test report.
technical_requirements_summary:
- Workloads: multi-tenant traffic routing (segmented by tenant id), heavy personalization + reranking spikes during campaigns.
- Models: mix of open LLMs (Llama-family) + custom fine-tuned reranker. Preference for quantized variants in Dedicated.
- Targets: sustained min tokens/sec = 12k, p95 latency < 250ms for short prompts, concurrency cap 20 per tenant route.
- Capacity planning: reserve enough GPUs to handle sustained rate plus 30% headroom for background batch jobs.
- Observability: token-level breakdown, per-route latency heatmaps, KV cache hit rates.
- Security: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 + contract-level audit logging.

commercial_notes:
- Price sensitivity: mid-high; prefer fixed committed units to control unit economics.
- Negotiation points: guaranteed min tokens/sec (primary), burst billing model (secondary), and GPU equivalence definition (how we count A100-vs-other).
- Asked to include rollback & fallback policy to hosted model for emergency overflow but must be opt-in; they want deterministic isolation by default.
- Proposed rebate/credits if throughput guarantee not met tied to monthly bill.
